text.tspan: Introduction
Results
Method
•Current options are expensive to
develop and manufacture. They require
a high degree of specialization and
suffer from itchyness and poor ventilation.
•Inflatable braces are cheap, simple
to manufacture, and easy to customize,
which makes them suitable for use in places
without access to advanced equipment.
•Developed a process to make a tailored inflatable arthritis hand
brace without the need for advanced tools such as 3D-scanners.
•Cell structure test results
•Prototypes
•TPU-Nylon sealing
•Experimented with different cell structures
•Analyzed shrinkage factor of different cell structures
•Developed blender program that generates hand brace
given 5 hand measurements as parameters
PROCESS HERE
This process can be developed further. Areas of possible
improvement include the generative blender program and the
cell structure of the brace. Given more time, the shrinking ratios
of the cells could be tested more thoroughly. This would also
allow for the shrinkage factors to be incorporated into the
design, to compensate for the change in size when the brace is
inflated.
The current cell structure is designed to support the thumb
joint, as well as the rest of the hand, but without input from
experts, this part of the design remains somewhat of a
guessing game. This is another area where the brace could be
improved.
Finally, some notes on the diagram shown in Results.
Discussion
Levi de Koning, Ivan Snel, Dorus Vrolijk, Eladje Barry
